newsitem.title: UK: INSTANT VIEW - UK August industry output data.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW - UK August industry output data.

text.p: Following is a selection of economists' reactions to UK data showing August industrial production fell 0.4 pct month/month and was unchanged year/year, while manufacturing output was down 0.3 percent m/m and down 0.9 percent respectively.
The Reuters forecast was industrial production +0.4% m/m and +0.9 % y/y, manufacturing output +0.4% m/m and -0.1% y/y
"I think it is disappointing, particularly because it flies in the face of survey evidence which has suggested recently that we should be seeing a slightly stronger recovery."

"However, it should be said that we have seen quite a chequered pattern of manufacturing output growth this year -- one month it's been down, the next month it's been up. That pattern has continued this month, with a decline after quite a sizeable increase in July. It's still a very flat picture overall."

"It is rather surprising. We had thought that the stock mountain had been wound down quite significantly and we would begin to see the benefit of strong consumer spending cutting on through to manufacturing output. It hasn't happened, the sector still looks quite weak -- rather bad news, I think, for the Conservatives just before their party conference. It does suggest this sector is now lagging very seriously behind the service sector."

"Weaker than expected. This comes as a disappointment in light of much more bullish survey data from the CBI and CIPS and should give a lift to both short sterling and gilts. Few likely to see the report as opening the door to a cut in base rate -- output is a lagging indicator of demand and most of the indicators of consumer behaviour have become much more positive. Nonetheless, still suggests that either manufacturers are wary about the sustainability or pace of the recovery in hand, or that the upturn is too concentrated in particular industries."
